newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egyptian shares fall due to profit taking.
newsitem.headline: Egyptian shares fall due to profit taking.

text.p: Egyptian share prices fell slightly on Wednesday mainly because of profit-taking in the dominant milling sector, brokers said.
The Capital Market Authority (CMA) all-share index closed 0.2 points down at 287.76 on turnover of 38.08 million pounds ($11.2 million).
"Profit taking in the milling sector had an impact on the whole market," said Hany Hosny, financial analyst at brokers Megavest.
But the current trend did not affect the rocketing price of Heliopolis Housing and Development, which ended 52.00 pounds up at 400.00 after shares worth 3.23 million pounds changed hands.
"I do not understand why this share goes up to such level," Hosny said. "I think it will fall very quickly after the general assembly decides later this month a 9.00 pound dividend."
There is still, however, heavy demand for the share, said Sherif Refaat of Thebes.
Recent increases in Medinet Nasr Housing and Development are justified, Hosny said. The share closed at 295.00 pounds, down 5.00.
The favourite milling sector ended mixed. East Delta Flour Mills, the second most active share, fell 2.00 to 50.50 but Upper Egypt Flour Mills ended 0.20 up at 69.00 pounds.
Central and West Delta Mills and North Cairo Flour Mills ended unchanged at 82.00 and 131.25 pounds respectively.
The CMA index for openly traded firms fell to 433.92 from 434.95 on Tuesday and the index for rarely traded "closed" firms rose to 202.07 from 202.01.
Of a total 80 shares traded, 27 fell and 14 rose while the rest closed unchanged.
